title: Console walkthrough: Usage analytics, per-route dashboards, cost breakdown - Lakeside Retail
summary: AE+SE walked Lakeside through Redwood Console usage analytics, per-route dashboards, and cost breakdown. Customer asked about per-route cost allocation, attribution to teams, and dedicated vs hosted economics. Security and SSO were raised; next steps: pricing, security pack, pilot benchmarks.
transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-03-04 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~55m
Attendees: Jordan K (Redwood AE), Priya D (Redwood SE), Maya P (Lakeside Head of ML), Tom R (CTO), Sandra L (Finance)
Recording link: https://redwood.app/meetings/ff-20260304-7892 (shared)

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone thanks for joining on time um i'll kick off, for folks who don't know me i'm jordan kim, AE for the account, with priya our solutions engineer.
[00:18] Priya: hi all, thanks  excited to walk through the console today, we'll focus on usage analytics, per-route dashboards and the cost breakdown view you asked about in the email.
[00:30] Maya: great, thanks. quick context  we run inference for search ranking and personalized recommendations, want per-team cost visibility and to understand how batching and KV cache reduce token costs.
[00:45] Tom: also we have strict SSO and SOC2 requirements, and finance is worried about surprise overages.
[00:55] Jordan: understood, we'll show guardrails, quotas and the per-route billing attribution and then go into model-level breakdowns.
[01:15] Priya: jumping into the console  opening the Usage Analytics page  you can see total tokens by day, broken into generation vs embeddings; note the chart on the right shows cost by model family, we auto-normalize to token units.
[01:40] Priya: (screen) here is the per-route dashboard, each route is its own dashboard with latency percentiles, error rates, model version, and cost per 1k tokens. you can change the window to 7/30/90 days.
[02:05] Maya: are these costs actual invoice-backed numbers or modeled estimates?
[02:12] Priya: good q  base numbers are our best estimates derived from token usage and model perf profiles, for hosted accounts invoice = estimate. for Dedicated you get exact commit pricing plus token overheads. sometimes transcription notes say "invoice equals estimate"  point being, we provide both modeled and invoice views.
[02:40] Tom: how do we attribute costs to teams? we have product, growth and platform teams using routes.
[02:48] Priya: routes map to projects; you can tag routes with team labels and we export per-tag cost. there's also a CSV export and a billing API endpoint to pull per-route allocation into your internal chargeback system. (link: /docs/billing/export)
[03:10] Sandra: and what about multi-model fallbacks  if a route falls back from a larger model to a cheaper one, does the dashboard show that shift?
[03:20] Priya: yes, the timeline shows model mix per route; cost breakdown shows the percentage of tokens by model variant and you can filter to show fallback events.
[03:36] Jordan: quick demo of a route  look at Route: "search-ranking-prod"  latency p50/p95, tokens per request, and the estimated cost per request. see the spike on Feb 25, we annotated it with an inciden ticket.
[04:00] Maya: small nit  token calc seems off for our 8k context run, does the console account for prompt+response + KV cache savings?
[04:10] Priya: yes, by default we show raw token consumption; if you enable KV cache and prefix caching, the dashboard will show normalized cost with cache savings applied. there's a toggle "apply caching adjustments". also note our optimizer suggests batching sizes given your latency SLO to reduce token overhead.
[04:40] Tom: how do you recommend we set batching for low-latency search? we need p95 < 120ms.
[04:50] Priya: for search ranking with short prompts, smaller batch sizes but continuous tail batching works well  our Optimize tool suggests batch size 8 with a micro-batching window of 20ms for that SLO, results in 18% token overhead reduction in our bench. we can run a live pilot to validate.
[05:20] Sandra: finance  how are reserved capacity commits shown? we want to compare Hosted per-token vs Dedicated reserved monthly.
[05:30] Jordan: in the Cost Breakdown page there's a compare view: "Hosted vs Dedicated"  you can input expected token profile and we project monthly cost under hosted per-token rates and under a set of Dedicated commit sizes with unit costs. we'll attach a sample spreadsheet.
[05:50] Priya: (shares spreadsheet link) https://redwood.app/share/lakeside-cost-model-EXAMPLE  this spreadsheet pulls per-route token estimates and runs scenarios.
[06:05] Sandra: okay send that to us. also procurement needs SOC2 Type II docs and SSO certs.
[06:12] Jordan: we'll include our security pack, SOC2 report, and SAML docs.
[06:20] Maya: with private deployment (VPC) can we still see the same Console metrics?
[06:28] Priya: yes, Private offers the same telemetry; the control plane will show aggregated metrics, and for on-prem we can ship a telemetry forwarder. small transcription glitch  sometimes our notes say "telemetry forwarder v s a p "  meaning we have a forwarder you can run.
[06:50] Tom: are logs and audit trails available for compliance? we need per-token lineage and request-level audit for 90 days.
[06:58] Priya: audit logs are available, request-level traces can be retained per your retention policy; we have retention tiers and can integrate with your Splunk or S3 archival.
[07:15] Jordan: returning to cost details  per-route cost breakdown shows cost by model, by route, and by team tag, plus a drilldown to sample requests contributing most tokens.
[07:30] Maya: show me an example of the drilldown.
[07:36] Priya: (screen) here's a drilldown  top 10 requests by tokens, you can click into request payloads, redactions are applied by default to PII. note: redaction isn't perfect in transcript, sometimes we show placeholders like [REDACTED-EMAIL].
[08:05] Sandra: curious about anomaly detection  unexpected spikes flagged?
[08:10] Priya: built-in anomaly detection flags deviance in token churn and cost per route; you can set thresholds and receive Slack/email alerts and auto-throttle options.
[08:30] Tom: what about model quantization and its effect on cost  do you show per-quantized-variant cost?
[08:36] Priya: we show model variant costs, including quantized variants. the model catalog indicates perf profiles for each quantization and we propagate that into estimates.
[08:55] Maya: any gotchas for recommendation workloads (longer context)?
[09:00] Priya: long context increases memory pressure and will shift kernel selection; console will surface expected throughput drop and associated cost. we recommend KV caching and prefix caching for recommendation flows to reduce repeated prompt overhead.
[09:20] Jordan: (note) Maya, you mentioned wanting attribution at product-feature level, not just team; you can attach metadata to requests and ingestion pipeline will roll that up.
[09:35] Maya: good. also can we get daily cost emails per product manager?
[09:40] Priya: yes, alerting and scheduled reports can be scoped to tags and delivered to emails or Slack channels.
[09:52] Sandra: procurement asks about penalty/SLAs for Dedicated.
[09:58] Jordan: Dedicated has SLA-backed throughput and latency with credits for missed SLOs; we'll include the SLA addendum in the pack.
[10:12] Tom: security review  we need KMS integration for keys and HSM support.
[10:18] Priya: we support customer-managed KMS and HSM options, and private deployments can use your key infrastructure. we'll include the KMS integration guide.
[10:35] Jordan: quick pause  any immediate blockers for proceeding to pilot?
[10:42] Maya: budget sign-off pending, procurement needs the docs.
[10:46] Sandra: finance needs cost model with realistic heavy-week scenario.
[10:50] Jordan: we'll run a heavy-week simulation in the spreadsheet and include a conservative forecast.
[11:05] Priya: let's demo the Compare view  selecting three routes and toggling caching and batching to show cost delta  see the chart: caching reduces estimated monthly cost by ~22% for recommendations route.
[11:30] Maya: that's promising. can we schedule an in-depth performance deep-dive to validate p95 numbers?
[11:38] Priya: yes SE-led deep dive; we typically run a 2-week POC with a small subset of traffic or replayed traffic to validate throughput and cost.
[11:52] Tom: replaying traffic  do you provide replay tooling or do we need to send logs?
[11:58] Priya: we have a replay harness, you can export sample requests and we can run them in a sandbox. we'll provide instructions in the bench guide.
[12:10] Sandra: and billing during pilot  is there a trial credit or how does that work?
[12:16] Jordan: we offer pilot credits for hosted and will work on a short-term Dedicated eval pricing if needed. we'll include options in the proposal.
[12:30] Maya: last question  how granular is the per-request redaction? we have PCI/PHI concerns for certain fields.
[12:38] Priya: redaction rules are configurable; for PHI we recommend private deployment and stricter retention. we'll include a compliance checklist.
[12:50] Jordan: great  recap and next steps.
[12:55] Jordan: action items  we'll send pricing, security pack, bench guide and the cost-model spreadsheet; SE to kick off replay harness details; schedule pilot kickoff once procurement clears.
[13:10] Maya: thanks, that works. we'll aim to confirm SSO and procurement timeline by Friday.
[13:20] Tom: thanks everyone, bye.
[13:22] Jordan: thanks all, bye.

Note: transcript contains small ASR artifacts and speaker label mismatches typical of call export.
